# Domain boundaries and prioritized split plan

**Status:** Active
**Owner:** Workslip maintainers
**Source of truth:** [`dependency-map.md`](dependency-map.md) (generated by `node tools/depmap/depmap.mjs`) plus git churn
**Review cadence:** After each boundary split, or when the dependency map changes materially
**Tracking:** [WOR-443](https://linear.app/workslip/issue/WOR-443) — blocked by WOR-442 (module contract), which must land before code moves

This page records where the business domains live in the codebase today, which boundaries are blurred, and in what order to split them. It intentionally ranks by evidence (coupling, change frequency, customer value), not by folder aesthetics. No big-bang rewrite; every split migrates behind existing contracts.

## Business domain → code mapping

The product's business domains and where each one currently lives. "Embedded in" means the domain has no boundary of its own today — it is a latent seam inside a larger module.

| Business domain | Backend (Application) | Frontend feature | Boundary today |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Job | `Jobs` | `jobs` | Own module, but acts as central orchestrator (fan-in 4, fan-out 4) |
| Worksheet (time tracking) | `Worksheets` | `worksheets` | Own module; bidirectional cycle with `Jobs` |
| Assignment | embedded in `Jobs` (`JobAssignmentService`) | embedded in `jobs` | Latent seam |
| Organization (tenant) | `Organizations` | `settings` / `superadmin` | Own module, clean (fan-in 0) |
| Filial | embedded in `Organizations` + `Jobs` | embedded | Latent seam; see `domain-and-dataflows.md` |
| Approval | embedded in `Jobs` (status transitions) | embedded in `jobs` | Latent seam |
| Billing / Costing | embedded in `Jobs` (costing paths) + Infra PDF generators | embedded in `jobs` reports | Latent seam; see ADR 0008 (job costing billing basis) |
| Rate / Pricing | embedded in `Jobs` / `Users` | embedded | Latent seam |
| Customer | `Customers` | `customers` | Own module backend; frontend leaks into `jobs` (7 cross-feature imports) |

Cross-cutting (not business domains, deliberately shared): `Auth` (fan-in 7 — the sanctioned dependency direction is *toward* Auth), `Notifications`, `Images`, `Common`, Domain models, Infrastructure.

## Evidence snapshot

Numbers from the generated dependency map and 6-month git churn (file-change counts). Regenerate the map after each split; churn command below.

| Boundary problem | Evidence | Churn (6 mo) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Jobs` is the orchestrator hub | fan-in 4 / fan-out 4, imports Auth+Users+Worksheets+Notifications; `JobService.cs` 1,153 LOC | FE `jobs` 737, BE `Jobs` 282 — by far the hottest code |
| `Jobs` ↔ `Worksheets` cycle | Jobs→Worksheets 4 file refs, Worksheets→Jobs 3 | BE `Worksheets` 50 |
| `Jobs` ↔ `Notifications` cycle | 1 ref each way | BE `Notifications` 33 |
| FE `customers` → `jobs` leak | 7 cross-feature imports | FE `customers` 56 |
| FE `users` ↔ `superadmin` cycle | 1 ref each way | FE `users` 59, `superadmin` 59 |
| `SqlDbContext` monolith | 1,625 LOC, all entity mappings in one file | schema churn tracked via migrations |

```bash
git log --since="6 months ago" --name-only --pretty=format: -- 'src/BE/WorkslipApi/Workslip.Application' 'src/FE/src/features' | grep -v '^$' | sed -E 's#^src/BE/WorkslipApi/Workslip.Application/([^/]+)/.*#BE:\1#; s#^src/FE/src/features/([^/]+)/.*#FE:\1#' | grep -E '^(BE|FE):' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20
```

## Prioritized splits

Ranked by coupling × change frequency × customer risk. Each split is a separate Linear issue; none start before WOR-442 defines the module contract they migrate onto.

### 1. Break the `Jobs` ↔ `Worksheets` cycle (backend)

The only true bidirectional Application dependency between two business domains, and both sides are hot. Direction to keep: Worksheets may know about Jobs (a worksheet belongs to job context); Jobs must not reach into Worksheets. Invert the 4 Jobs→Worksheets file refs behind an interface owned by Jobs (or a domain event), per the WOR-442 contract.

**Measurable goal:** `Jobs -> Worksheets` edge reaches 0 file refs in the dependency map; Jobs fan-out drops from 4 to 3. No API contract changes.

### 2. Stop the frontend `customers` → `jobs` leak

7 cross-feature imports make `customers` un-shippable independently of `jobs` and drag customer screens along on jobs churn (737 changes/6 mo). Move the shared pieces to `src/FE/src/components`/`lib` only if genuinely shared UI; otherwise duplicate the trivial ones. No junk-drawer `shared/` folder.

**Measurable goal:** `customers -> jobs` edge reaches 0; frontend cross-feature import total drops from 16 toward ≤ 5 (remaining edges get their own issues).

### 3. Extract Approval + Assignment seams out of `JobService`

`JobService.cs` (1,153 LOC) mixes CRUD, status transitions (Approval domain), multi-assignment logic (Assignment domain) and costing. Carve along the domains the business plans name — Approval and Assignment first, since both already have distinct rules documented in `domain-and-dataflows.md`. This is a within-module split: cheaper, no contract risk, prepares Billing/Rate extraction later.

**Measurable goal:** `JobService.cs` under ~500 LOC; Approval and Assignment logic in named services with their own tests; no authorization behavior change (existing tenant/filial tests stay green).

### 4. Split `SqlDbContext` mappings by domain

1,625 LOC single file forces every domain change through one hotspot and hides ownership. Mechanical split into per-domain `IEntityTypeConfiguration` classes; no schema change, no migration.

**Measurable goal:** `SqlDbContext.cs` under ~200 LOC; mapping files grouped per domain; `dotnet build` and persistence tests unchanged.

### 5. Untangle FE `users` ↔ `superadmin` and `settings` → `images`

Smaller leaks; same treatment as split 2. Bundle into one issue.

**Measurable goal:** both cycles/edges at 0 in the map.

## Frontend stylesheet migration (WOR-475)

`src/FE/src/App.css` is still a legacy catch-all spanning shell, jobs, worksheets, attestation, users, invites, login and time overview. New styling must not make that file larger: `npm run check:app-css-budget` enforces a migration ceiling during the normal frontend build.

Existing ownership seams are the model for the migration:

| Styling domain | Owner path | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| App shell desktop refinements | `components/layouts/AppLayout.desktop.css` | Keep selectors tied to `AppLayout` markup here. |
| App shell focus/keyboard behavior | `components/layouts/AppLayout.focus.css` | Keep focus visibility and editable-control navigation behavior here. |
| Job wizard theme | `features/jobs/jobWizardTheme.css` | Keep wizard-specific visual rules in the jobs feature. |
| Superadmin organization session | `features/superadmin/organizationSession.css` | Keep session/banner behavior in the superadmin feature. |
| Legacy mixed rules | `App.css` | No new domain styling; only shrink this file as owners absorb selectors. |

Next extraction order is deliberately risk-based rather than based on selector count:

1. shell/header/bottom-navigation rules → `components/layouts/` while preserving mobile safe-area and focus behavior;
2. worksheet/calendar/time-entry rules → `features/worksheets/`;
3. job list/card/report/attestation rules → `features/jobs/`;
4. invite/login rules → their authentication/invitation owners;
5. generic form/select primitives only after verifying they are truly shared components rather than coincidentally similar selectors.

Each extraction must remove the original selectors in the same change; temporary duplicate selector blocks do not count as a split. Run frontend lint/tests/build and spot-check keyboard focus, reduced-motion and mobile/desktop breakpoints before merging an extraction.

## Non-goals (restating WOR-443)

- No full rewrite, no microservices without a documented need.
- File/folder renames are never the goal; a split only counts when the dependency map shows less coupling.
- Shared code moves only when it is genuinely shared domain/infrastructure — no generic junk drawers.
- No cross-tenant or authorization regressions: every split re-runs the tenant/filial persistence tests before merge.

## Working agreement

1. Land WOR-442 (module contract) first; splits 1–5 each get their own Linear issue referencing this plan.
2. Before a split: run `node tools/depmap/depmap.mjs`, commit the map as the baseline.
3. After a split: regenerate, and quote the before/after edge counts in the PR description. `--check` keeps the committed map honest in review.
